la:other:Samnium.html:
Samnĭum, ii, n.
contr. from Sabinium, from Sabini: ab Sabinis orti Samnites, Müll.
,
an ancient country of Italy, in the neighborhood of Latium, whose inhabitants were an offshoot from the Sabines, ; ; ; ; —Hence,
Samnīs (collat. form of the nom.Samnītis, Cato ap. ; ), ītis, adj., of or belonging to Samnium, Samnite: ager,: exercitus,: bellum,: ursae,: habitator Samnitis (terrae), Prud. στεφ. 11, 207.— Subst., in plur.: Samnītes, ĭum (gen. Samnitum, ; but cf. Samnitium, Orell. N. cr.; and so usu. and very freq. in Liv., Plin., and Tac.), m., the inhabitants of Samnium, the Samnites, ; ; sq.; 8, 1 sq.; 9, 1 sq.; ; ; —Gr. acc. Samnităs, ; .—In sing.: Samnīs, ītis, m., collect., the Samnites, ; .—
Transf., the name of Samnites was also given to a class of gladiators who were armed with Samnite weapons, Müll.; ; ; ; ; .—So in sing.: Samnīs, Lucil. ap. ; and ap. de Or. 3, 23, 86.—
Samnītĭcus, a, um, adj., Samnite: bellum,; : vasa,.

la:other:Samothracia.html:
Sămŏthrācĭa, ae, f.,
Samothrace, an island near the coast of Thrace, famous for the mystic worship of the Cabiri, now Samothraki, ; ; ; Müll.; .—Also called Sămŏthrācē, ēs, f., ; ; ; Sămŏthrāca, ae, f., ; ; ; and Thrēïcĭa Să-mus or Sămos, after the Gr. θρηϊκίη Σάμος, ; .— Hence,
Sămŏthrācĭus, a, um, adj., Samothracian: ferrea (a kind of rings first made there), (cf. ): caepa,: insula, i. e. Samothrace, and, named from it, gemma, (Jahn, Samothraca). —
Sămŏthrāces, um, m., the inhabitants of Samothrace, the Samothracians, ; ; ; .—Also a dject.: Samothraces di,the Cabiri,. 1.; ; also absol.: jures licet et Samothracum Et nostrorum aras,.—
Sămŏthrācēnus, a, um, adj., Samothracian: Zocles,of Samothrace,.—
Sămŏthrācĭcus, a, um, adj., Samothracian: religiones,.—
Sămŏthrācus, a, um, adj., Samothracian: vates,.

la:noun:Samaria.html:
Sămărīa, ae, f., = Σαμάρεια (orig. Heb. ),
the middle district of Palestine, .—Hence,
Să-mărītae, ārum, m., the inhabitants of Samaria, the Samaritans, ; .—In sing.: Sămărī-tes, ae, m., a Samaritan, Hadr. ap. .—
Sămărītis, ĭdis, f., a Samaritan woman, ; ; .—
Sămărītānus, a, um, adj., Samaritan: via,.—In plur., the Samaritans, Esd. 4, 2.—
Sămărītĭcus, a, um, adj., Samaritan: mulier,.—
Sămă-rēus, a, um, adj., Samaritan: superstitio,.
